title: Industrial Alarm Monitoring
summary: A Raspberry Pi monitoring system bringing 40 alarm inputs, a local operator interface and network access into one application.
problem: Industrial operators need to see input states, understand alarm events and retain a useful history across local and networked workflows.
approach: Connected configurable AC/DC alarm inputs to a Raspberry Pi-based application.
Built a PyQt interface for input status and operator interaction.
Combined local event storage with network and web components for monitoring.
outcome: A monitoring-system implementation spanning hardware inputs, the operator interface and database-backed event records.
software: Local event storage & SQL Server integration

sections.title: Preserving the history behind an alarm
body: An indicator alone cannot explain what happened while an operator was away. This system combines live alarm visibility with stored records so events remain available for review after the initial indication.

sections.title: Standalone and networked operation
body: In standalone mode, the device monitors alarms and shutdowns, stores events locally and accepts physical operator commands. In networked mode, it connects to SQL Server and makes the event workflow available across the local network.

sections.title: Three ways to operate the system
body: The same alarm workflow is accessible through physical inputs, an HDMI interface and a browser. Operators can acknowledge and reset alarms, change channel titles and input modes, and configure the displayed alarms.

sections.title: Forty channels, one interface
body: The custom board provides 40 AC/DC input channels with optocoupler isolation and buffer circuitry. Configurable jumpers adapt the input arrangement. I developed the software and system integration; Mohammad Khodadadeh designed the hardware and Hossein Aalamshahi managed the project.

sections.title: Configuration and service tools
body: The browser interface brings together general settings, USB-device information, network status, saved events and live alarm controls. Local event lists and export functions support maintenance and review.

system.label: Industrial alarm inputs
system.description: Forty configurable AC/DC input channels feed the custom board.

system.label: Isolation and acquisition
system.description: The board uses optocouplers and buffer circuitry; Raspberry Pi GPIO acquires the input states.

system.label: Event handling
system.description: Python processes alarm events and operator acknowledge/reset commands.

system.label: Local persistence
system.description: SQLite supports local records when operating standalone.

system.label: Operator interfaces
system.description: PyQt/HDMI and the local HTTP interface expose state, events and settings.

system.label: Network records
system.description: The networked mode connects to SQL Server for central access.

strength: 40 alarm channels. Three ways to operate.
contribution: I developed the Python monitoring software, PyQt operator interface and integration of hardware input states, local event records and networked access. The custom input-board hardware was designed by Mohammad Khodadadeh; Hossein Aalamshahi managed the project.
result: A monitoring-system implementation spanning hardware inputs, the operator interface and database-backed event records.
decisionNotes: The implementation supports standalone records alongside networked SQL Server access. Physical acknowledge/reset inputs, PyQt on HDMI and a local browser interface provide three operator paths.
validationNotes: Original hardware photographs, interface views and archival recordings document the monitoring implementation. They show the device and operator workflow; the archive does not provide a measured reliability or deployment study.
